recipes.title: Crispy Chipotle Tofu Tacos with Lime Slaw
recipes.bodyMd:
# Crispy Chipotle Tofu Tacos with Lime Slaw
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-23

## Attributes
cuisine: Mexican | format: tacos | technique: air-fried | effort: moderate
components: tofu, cabbage, corn tortillas
flavors: smoky, spicy, tangy | textures: crispy, crunchy
nut-free, dairy-free, fish-free

## Time
Prep: 20 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: ~40 min | Difficulty: Easy–Moderate

## Ingredients
**Tofu**
- 14 oz (400 g) extra-firm tofu, pressed 10–15 min, cut into ¾-inch cubes
- 1 tbsp olive oil or avocado oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1–1½ tsp chipotle powder (or 1 minced chipotle in adobo + 1 tsp sauce; check label for nuts)
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ¾ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp kosher salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- Juice of ½ lime

**Slaw**
- 3 cups shredded green cabbage (or coleslaw mix without nuts)
- ½ cup shredded carrot
- ¼ cup chopped cilantro
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp maple syrup or agave (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste

**To serve**
- 6 small corn tortillas (warmed)
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- Lime wedges
- Hot sauce (optional; check nut-free)

## Instructions
1. Press tofu, cube, and pat dry. Toss with oil, cornstarch, chipotle, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until coated.
2. Air fry at 400°F (200°C) for 14–18 minutes, shaking halfway, until edges are deep golden and crisp. (Pan method: nonstick skillet over medium-high, 8–10 min, turning.) Finish with lime juice.
3. Toss slaw ingredients; rest 5 minutes.
4. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet 20–30 seconds per side.
5. Build tacos: tofu, slaw, avocado, lime. Serve immediately.

## Nutrition perspective
Protein-rich, high-fiber, vegetable-forward; balanced spice and fat from avocado.

## Substitutions
Tempeh cubes work in place of tofu (same seasoning). Skip chipotle for smoked paprika only if heat is too much.

recipes.title: Blackstone Miso-Ginger Salmon with Blistered Bok Choy
recipes.bodyMd:
# Blackstone Miso-Ginger Salmon with Blistered Bok Choy
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-23

## Attributes
cuisine: Japanese-inspired | format: plated entrée | technique: griddled | effort: moderate
components: salmon, bok choy, rice
flavors: umami, savory, garlicky | textures: tender, charred
nut-free, dairy-free; contains fish

## Time
Prep: 15 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: ~35 min | Difficulty: Moderate

## Ingredients
**Salmon & glaze**
- 2 salmon fillets (5–6 oz / 140–170 g each), skin-on preferred, pin bones removed
- 1½ tbsp white or yellow miso (check nut-free)
- 1 tbsp mirin (or 1 tsp maple syrup + 1 tsp rice vinegar)
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 small garlic clove, grated
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (seeds, not nuts — OK)
- Neutral oil for the griddle
- Salt and pepper

**Greens & rice**
- 2–3 baby bok choy, halved lengthwise, rinsed well
- 1 cup dry jasmine or short-grain rice, cooked per package (~3 cups cooked)
- Lime or lemon wedges
- Optional: sliced scallions, toasted sesame seeds

## Instructions
1. Cook rice so it finishes with the fish.
2. Whisk miso, mirin, soy/tamari, ginger, garlic, and sesame oil into a smooth glaze. Pat salmon dry; lightly salt flesh side. Brush glaze on flesh.
3. Preheat Blackstone flat-top to medium-high. Oil lightly.
4. Place salmon skin-side down. Cook 4–5 minutes until skin crisps and flesh is opaque ~⅔ up the side. Flip carefully; cook 2–3 minutes more until just opaque and flakes easily (internal ~125–130°F / 52–54°C for medium). Brush remaining glaze in the last minute. Rest 2 minutes off heat.
5. On a hot zone, oil lightly and blister bok choy cut-side down 2–3 minutes until charred, then flip 1–2 minutes until stems tender-crisp. Season with a pinch of salt and a drop of soy if desired.
6. Plate rice, salmon, and bok choy. Scallions, sesame seeds, citrus wedge optional.

**No Blackstone:** Same glaze; skillet medium-high, skin-side down first; broil bok choy or sauté.

## Nutrition perspective
High protein, omega-3 rich; vegetable side keeps the plate balanced. Comfort-level richness without heaviness.

## Substitutions
Firm white fish (cod, halibut) works; reduce cook time. Broccolini instead of bok choy.

recipes.title: Coconut Chickpea & Spinach Curry with Basmati
recipes.bodyMd:
# Coconut Chickpea & Spinach Curry with Basmati
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-23

## Attributes
cuisine: Indian-inspired | format: curry | technique: simmered | effort: easy
components: chickpeas, spinach, coconut milk, rice
flavors: aromatic, creamy, mildly spicy | textures: creamy, tender
nut-free, dairy-free, fish-free — no cashew cream, no nut garnishes

## Time
Prep: 15 min | Cook: 25 min | Total: ~40 min | Difficulty: Easy

## Ingredients
- 1 tbsp coconut oil or olive oil
- 1 small yellow onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1½ tsp curry powder (confirm nut-free)
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp turmeric
- ¼–½ tsp cayenne or chili flakes (optional)
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz / 400 ml) full-fat coconut milk
- ½ cup water or vegetable broth
- 4 cups baby spinach (about 4 oz / 115 g)
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Salt to taste
- ¾ cup dry basmati rice, cooked
- Fresh cilantro for serving (optional)
- Do **not** add cashews, almonds, or peanut garnish

## Instructions
1. Start rice.
2. Warm oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Soften onion 5–6 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.
3. Stir in curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne 30 seconds until fragrant. Add tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
4. Add chickpeas, coconut milk, and water/broth. Simmer gently 12–15 minutes until slightly thickened. Mash a few chickpeas against the pot for body.
5. Fold in spinach until wilted, 1–2 minutes. Off heat, add lime juice and salt. Taste: more lime or salt as needed.
6. Serve over basmati with cilantro if using.

## Nutrition perspective
High-fiber, vegetable-forward comfort food; plant protein from chickpeas; coconut makes it satisfying without dairy.

## Substitutions
Kale or frozen spinach (squeezed dry) instead of baby spinach. Light coconut milk for a lighter bowl (sauce will be thinner).

recipes.title: Blackstone Ginger-Scallion Broccoli & Shiitake Rice Bowls
recipes.bodyMd:
# Blackstone Ginger-Scallion Broccoli & Shiitake Rice Bowls
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-24

## Attributes
cuisine: Chinese-inspired | format: bowl | technique: griddled / stir-fried | effort: moderate
components: broccoli, shiitake, rice, scallions
flavors: savory, gingery, garlicky, umami | textures: charred, tender-crisp
nut-free, dairy-free, fish-free — no peanut sauce, no cashew garnish

## Time
Prep: 15 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: ~35 min | Difficulty: Moderate

## Ingredients
**Rice**
- 1 cup dry jasmine rice, cooked per package (~3 cups cooked)

**Veggies & aromatics**
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into bite-size florets (about 4 cups)
- 8 oz (225 g) shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, caps sliced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced thin (optional color)
- 4 scallions, whites and greens separated, thinly sliced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- Neutral oil for the griddle (avocado, canola, or grapeseed)

**Sauce**
- 3 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp maple syrup or sugar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (seeds, not nuts — OK)
- ½ tsp chili flakes or chili crisp without nuts (optional)
- Pinch of white or black pepper

**Finish**
- Lime wedges
- Optional: toasted sesame seeds (not nuts)
- Do **not** add peanuts, peanut sauce, or cashews

## Instructions
1. Start rice so it finishes with the vegetables.
2. Whisk sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Set aside.
3. Preheat Blackstone flat-top to medium-high. Oil lightly.
4. Spread broccoli in a hot zone; cook 4–5 minutes, tossing occasionally, until charred in spots and tender-crisp. Push to a cooler edge.
5. Oil again if needed. Add shiitakes (and bell pepper if using). Cook 3–4 minutes until browned and softened. Add scallion whites, garlic, and ginger; cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant — don’t burn the garlic.
6. Pull everything together on the griddle. Pour sauce over; toss 30–60 seconds until glossy and lightly reduced.
7. Bowl rice, pile vegetables on top, scatter scallion greens. Lime wedge and sesame seeds optional.

**No Blackstone:** Use a large cast-iron or wok over high heat; same order (broccoli first, then mushrooms, aromatics last).

## Nutrition perspective
Vegetable-forward, high fiber; plant protein from mushrooms and whatever else you add. Satisfying without dairy or nuts. Light-to-moderate richness from sesame oil and char.

## Substitutions
Cremini or oyster mushrooms instead of shiitake. Snap peas or broccolini instead of broccoli. For more protein, add baked or air-fried extra-firm tofu cubes in the last toss (optional — tofu was probed yesterday).

recipes.title: Tomato-Basil White Bean Rigatoni
recipes.bodyMd:
# Tomato-Basil White Bean Rigatoni
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-24

## Attributes
cuisine: Italian | format: pasta | technique: stovetop simmer | effort: easy
components: rigatoni, white beans, tomato, basil, garlic
flavors: savory, herby, bright, garlicky | textures: al dente, saucy
nut-free, dairy-free, fish-free — no Parmesan, no cream, no nut pesto

## Time
Prep: 10 min | Cook: 25 min | Total: ~35 min | Difficulty: Easy

## Ingredients
- 8 oz (225 g) dry rigatoni (or penne / ziti)
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
- ½ tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
- 1 can (14.5 oz / 411 g) crushed or diced tomatoes
- 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) cannellini or great northern beans, drained and rinsed
- ½ tsp dried oregano
- Salt and black pepper
- 1 large handful fresh basil leaves, torn (or 1 tsp dried basil)
- 1 tsp lemon zest or a squeeze of lemon (optional brightness)
- Do **not** finish with Parmesan, butter, or pine-nut pesto

## Instructions
1. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook pasta until just shy of al dente (about 1 minute under package time). Reserve 1 cup pasta water; drain.
2. While pasta cooks: warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add garlic (and pepper flakes if using); cook 1–2 minutes until fragrant and just golden — not brown.
3. Add tomatoes, oregano, a pinch of salt, and a grind of pepper. Simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
4. Stir in beans. Mash ~¼ of them against the pan for a creamy body without dairy. Simmer 2–3 minutes.
5. Add drained pasta plus ¼–½ cup pasta water. Toss over medium heat 1–2 minutes until sauce clings. Add more pasta water if tight.
6. Off heat: fold in remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, torn basil, and lemon zest/juice if using. Taste for salt. Serve immediately.

## Nutrition perspective
Solid plant protein and fiber from beans; tomato and basil keep it bright. Comfort pasta without dairy heaviness.

## Substitutions
Chickpeas work if white beans are out (different from yesterday’s curry context). Spinach wilted into the sauce in the last minute is fine. Gluten-free short pasta if needed.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Lemon-Dill Cod with Potatoes & Green Beans
recipes.bodyMd:
# Sheet-Pan Lemon-Dill Cod with Potatoes & Green Beans
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-24

## Attributes
cuisine: Mediterranean | format: plated entrée | technique: sheet-pan roast | effort: easy
components: cod, potato, green beans, lemon, dill
flavors: bright, herby, citrus, savory | textures: flaky, crisp-roast
nut-free, dairy-free; contains fish — no butter, no cream sauce

## Time
Prep: 15 min | Cook: 30 min | Total: ~45 min | Difficulty: Easy

## Ingredients
**Vegetables**
- ¾ lb (340 g) baby potatoes, halved (or Yukon gold cut in ¾-inch chunks)
- 8 oz (225 g) green beans, trimmed
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp smoked or sweet paprika
- Salt and black pepper

**Fish**
- 2 cod fillets (5–6 oz / 140–170 g each), or other firm white fish (haddock, pollock)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon (½ for juice/zest, ½ sliced into rounds)
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh dill (or 1 tsp dried)
- 1 small garlic clove, grated or minced
- Pinch of salt and pepper

**Finish**
- Extra lemon wedges
- More fresh dill if you have it
- Do **not** finish with butter or creamy dill sauce (dairy)

## Instructions
1. Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large sheet pan with parchment if you like easier cleanup.
2. Toss potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread cut-side down. Roast 15 minutes.
3. Meanwhile, pat cod dry. Mix 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, 1 tbsp lemon juice, dill, garlic, salt, and pepper. Coat fillets.
4. Pull the pan out. Push potatoes to one side. Toss green beans with remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; add to the pan. Nestle cod in the open space; lay a lemon slice or two on each fillet.
5. Roast 12–15 minutes more until potatoes are tender, green beans blistered, and cod flakes easily (internal ~140°F / 60°C). Thick fillets may need 1–2 extra minutes; thin fillets less.
6. Plate with lemon wedges and a little more dill.

**Blackstone option (not required):** Roast potatoes in the oven; sear lemon-dill cod and blister green beans on a medium Blackstone flat-top for more char — only if you want the extra step.

## Nutrition perspective
High protein, relatively light richness; potatoes and green beans make a complete plate. Bright citrus-herb profile vs heavier glazes.

## Substitutions
Halibut or tilapia with adjusted cook time. Asparagus or broccolini instead of green beans. Sweet potato chunks instead of baby potatoes (may need a few more minutes before adding fish).

recipes.title: Crispy Falafel Pita Wraps with Lemon Cashew-Tahini
recipes.bodyMd:
# Crispy Falafel Pita Wraps with Lemon Cashew-Tahini
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-26

## Attributes
cuisine: Middle Eastern | format: wraps | technique: air-fried | effort: moderate
components: chickpeas, pita, cucumber, cashew tahini
flavors: herby, garlicky, tangy, savory | textures: crispy, creamy, crunchy
dairy-free, fish-free; contains cashews (permitted); no other nuts

## Time
Prep: 20 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: ~40 min | Difficulty: Moderate

## Ingredients
**Falafel**
- 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, drained, rinsed, patted very dry
- ½ small yellow onion, roughly chopped
- 2 garlic cloves
- ½ cup packed fresh parsley (or parsley + cilantro mix)
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp kosher salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ tsp baking powder
- 2–3 tbsp chickpea flour or all-purpose flour (just enough to hold)
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for coating before air fry)

**Lemon cashew-tahini sauce**
- ⅓ cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water 15 min, drained
- 2 tbsp tahini (sesame — OK; check label nut-free aside from sesame)
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 small garlic clove
- ¼–⅓ cup cold water (to thin)
- ¼ tsp salt, pinch cumin

**Wraps & salad**
- 4 small pita or flatbreads (warmed)
- 1 cup shredded romaine or cabbage
- 1 Persian cucumber, diced
- 1 Roma tomato, diced
- Pickled red onion or thin red onion slices (optional)
- Fresh mint or parsley to finish
- Do **not** add pine nuts, almonds, or dairy yogurt sauce

## Instructions
1. Soak cashews in hot water while you prep falafel.
2. Pulse chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper in a food processor until coarse and sticky — not a puree. Pulse in baking powder and flour until the mix holds when squeezed. Chill 5–10 minutes if soft.
3. Form 10–12 small patties (~1½ inch). Brush or toss lightly with olive oil. Air fry at 375°F (190°C) 12–16 minutes, flipping halfway, until deep golden and crisp outside. (Oven: 400°F / 200°C on a parchment-lined sheet, 18–22 min, flip halfway.)
4. Blend drained cashews, tahini, lemon, garlic, salt, cumin, and water until silky. Thin to drizzle consistency.
5. Warm pitas. Fill with greens, cucumber, tomato, onion, falafel, and generous cashew-tahini. Mint/parsley on top. Serve immediately.

## Nutrition perspective
High-fiber plant protein; cashew-tahini adds richness without dairy. Enjoyment-forward street-food format.

## Substitutions
Store-bought plain falafel mix only if dairy-/nut-free (except cashews if you add them separately). Hummus thinned with lemon works if skipping cashews — but this option is meant to probe the cashew exception.

recipes.title: Blackstone Korean Gochujang-Glazed Trout with Sesame Cucumber Salad
recipes.bodyMd:
# Blackstone Korean Gochujang-Glazed Trout with Sesame Cucumber Salad
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-26

## Attributes
cuisine: Korean-inspired | format: plated_entree | technique: griddled | effort: moderate
components: trout, cucumber, rice, gochujang
flavors: sweet-heat, savory, garlicky, bright | textures: flaky, crisp-skin, crunchy
dairy-free, nut-free; contains fish — no shellfish

## Time
Prep: 15 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: ~35 min | Difficulty: Moderate

## Ingredients
**Trout & glaze**
- 2 trout fillets (5–6 oz / 140–170 g each), skin-on preferred (or arctic char)
- 1½ tbsp gochujang (check label: no fish sauce with shellfish, no peanut)
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp maple syrup or brown sugar
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 small garlic clove, grated
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (seeds — OK)
- Neutral oil for the griddle
- Salt and pepper

**Sesame cucumber salad**
- 1 large English cucumber (or 2 Persian), thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp soy sauce or tamari
- ½ tsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp toasted sesame oil
- Pinch of salt and chili flakes
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

**To serve**
- ¾–1 cup dry jasmine rice, cooked (~2½–3 cups)
- 2 scallions, thinly sliced
- Lime wedges (optional)
- Do **not** add peanuts, peanut sauce, or butter

## Instructions
1. Start rice. Toss cucumber salad ingredients; chill while cooking.
2. Whisk gochujang, soy, maple, vinegar, ginger, garlic, and sesame oil into a glaze. Pat trout dry; lightly salt flesh. Brush glaze on flesh (reserve a spoonful for finish).
3. Preheat Blackstone flat-top to medium-high. Oil lightly.
4. Place trout skin-side down. Cook 3–4 minutes until skin crisps and flesh turns opaque ~⅔ up the side. Flip carefully; cook 1–2 minutes more until just flakes. Brush remaining glaze in the last 30 seconds. Rest 1–2 minutes off heat.
5. Plate rice, trout, and cucumber salad. Scallions and sesame seeds on top.

**No Blackstone:** Skillet medium-high, skin-side down first; same glaze timing. Broil 1 minute at the end if you want extra caramelization.

## Nutrition perspective
High-protein fish plate with cooling crunch; sweet-heat glaze for enjoyment without dairy or shellfish.

## Substitutions
Salmon works but this plan intentionally uses trout (vs prior salmon/cod). Firm white fish needs less glaze sweetness and shorter cook. Broccolini blistered on the side if you want a hot vegetable.

recipes.title: Moroccan Spiced Lentil & Roasted Carrot Tagine with Couscous
recipes.bodyMd:
# Moroccan Spiced Lentil & Roasted Carrot Tagine with Couscous
Version: 1 | Serves: 2 | Status: proposed 2026-09-26

## Attributes
cuisine: Moroccan-inspired | format: tagine | technique: simmered + roasted | effort: easy
components: lentils, carrots, couscous, warm spices
flavors: warm-spiced, savory, slightly sweet, bright | textures: tender, stew-y, fluffy
nut-free, dairy-free, fish-free — no almond garnish, no yogurt

## Time
Prep: 15 min | Cook: 30 min | Total: ~45 min | Difficulty: Easy

## Ingredients
**Roasted carrots**
- 3–4 medium carrots, cut on bias into ½-inch pieces
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp cumin
- Pinch cinnamon, salt, pepper

**Tagine stew**
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small yellow onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger (optional)
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp smoked or sweet paprika
- ¼ tsp cinnamon
- ¼ tsp turmeric
- Pinch cayenne (optional)
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- ¾ cup dry brown or green lentils, rinsed
- 1 can (14.5 oz / 411 g) diced tomatoes
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- ½ cup frozen peas (optional, last 5 min)
- Juice of ½ lemon
- Salt and black pepper
- Handful chopped cilantro or parsley

**Couscous**
- ¾ cup dry couscous (or quinoa if preferred)
- ¾ cup boiling water or broth + pinch salt + 1 tsp olive oil
- Do **not** finish with almonds, pine nuts, or dairy yogurt

## Instructions
1. Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss carrots with oil and spices; roast 18–22 minutes until caramelized at the edges.
2. Meanwhile, warm oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Soften onion 5–6 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Stir in cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, turmeric, and cayenne 30 seconds. Add tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
3. Add lentils, diced tomatoes, and broth. Bring to a simmer; cook uncovered 22–28 minutes until lentils are tender and stew thickens. Stir occasionally; add a splash of water if tight. Fold in peas for the last 5 minutes if using.
4. Pour boiling water/broth over couscous in a bowl; cover 5 minutes; fluff with fork and olive oil.
5. Stir roasted carrots and lemon juice into the stew. Salt to taste. Serve over couscous with herbs.

## Nutrition perspective
High-fiber plant meal; warm spices deliver comfort without cream or nuts. Easy weeknight stew format.

## Substitutions
Red lentils cook faster (~12–15 min) but go softer — fine for a thicker stew. Sweet potato cubes can roast with (or instead of) carrots. Quinoa or rice instead of couscous.
